subject: US Q1 regime under cross-asset divergence
claim: Within Q1-labeled periods, simultaneous cross-asset divergence and aligned systematic cutting are associated with weaker 10-day broad-equity outcomes than Q1 periods without that conjunction.
hypothesis: Within Q1-labeled periods, simultaneous cross-asset divergence and aligned systematic cutting are associated with weaker 10-day broad-equity outcomes than Q1 periods without that conjunction.
falsifier: Falsified if, after at least 25 independent events, the mean 10-day SPY excess outcome under the conjunction is not at least 1 percentage point below the Q1 no-conjunction baseline.

subject: Q2 cross-asset divergence
claim: When an equity Q2 regime is simultaneously contradicted by both FX-dollar and rates-credit legs, subsequent 21-day equity-regime persistence is lower than for Q2 observations without that dual contradiction.
hypothesis: When an equity Q2 regime is simultaneously contradicted by both FX-dollar and rates-credit legs, subsequent 21-day equity-regime persistence is lower than for Q2 observations without that dual contradiction.
falsifier: Reject if, after at least 30 independent Q2 observations, dual-contradiction cases do not reduce 21-day Q2 persistence by at least 10 percentage points versus other Q2 observations.
